Alloy ingots weighing 50 g were prepared using a vacuum-arc melting unit equipped with a water-cooled copper hearth and a non-consumable tungsten electrode under an inert argon (Ar) atmosphere. Table 1 gives the alloy ingot compositions and their nomenclature used in this work. High-purity elements (99.99 + ) were used for alloy preparations. To improve the compositional homogeneity, the ingots were flipped and re-melted five times.
The alloys were subsequently cast in the form of 3 mm diameter rods using a vacuum suction casting unit equipped with a water-cooled split copper mold.
The cast rods were annealed at 1200 ◦C for 50 h in a tubular furnace operating under vacuum of 10^4 Pa, followed by water quenching.
The solution-treated alloys were aged at 900 ◦C for 50 h, followed by immediate water quenching.
